title: Keyturn Guest Protection Plan: Measuring the Days of Cover on an Election
content:
**The measure.** The covered days of a Keyturn Guest Protection Plan election are the reserved hours of the
trip divided by the hours in a day and rounded up to a whole day, never fewer than the minimum cover days, and
never more than the cover ceiling.

**The figures the measure uses.** The hours in a day are 24. The minimum cover days are 1. The cover ceiling is
30 days.

**Where the quantity comes from.** The reserved hours are the hours the booking reserves, carried on the
Keyturn Trip Booking the election belongs to.

**The order in which the measure is taken.** The reserved hours are divided by the hours in a day first and the
result carried up to the next whole day; the figure so reached is then raised to the minimum cover days if it
falls below them, and finally held down to the cover ceiling if it stands above it.

## Worked on hypothetical figures

| Reserved hours on the booking | Divided by the hours in a day | Carried up to a whole day | Days of cover |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | Rather under half a day | 1 | 1 |
| 50 | Rather over two days | 3 | 3 |
| 172 | Rather over seven days | 8 | 8 |
| 900 | Rather over thirty-seven days | 38 | 30 |

A booking reserving 50 hours divides into 24 twice with 2 hours left over, so the figure carried up to the next
whole day is 3. Three days stands above the minimum cover days of 1 and below the cover ceiling of 30, so the
election carries 3 days of cover. A booking reserving 900 hours reaches 38 whole days once carried up,
which stands above the ceiling of 30, and the election carries 30 days of cover.

A booking reserving 10 hours reaches 1 whole day once carried up, which is already the minimum cover days, so
the election carries 1 day of cover.
